proposals.name: Concrete regulatory exposure, not generic organizational self-description
proposals.instruction: Score how concretely the text establishes that the commenter is a party this rule actually operates on. 10 = the comment names the specific assets, products, operations, filings, acreage, catch, or populations the rule reaches (a fleet count, an affected product line, a form the commenter must file, the crop under the restriction), so the exposure is checkable from the text alone. 5 = an affected-industry claim is asserted only in general terms. 0 = identity is conveyed solely by mission statement, membership counts, or a roster of affiliates, with no link drawn between who the commenter is and what the rule does to them. Judge only the linkage between identity and rule; do not reward prestige, org size, or professional letterhead.
proposals.rationale: R52 states the NPRM affects twenty-one of United's own 747-400s; R27 is Boeing concurring on an AD against parts on its own airframe; R50 is a grower writing from inside the exact volume restriction; R11 is Sanofi naming the insulin products that transition under the provision. All four are dense-high and card-low. On the other side R15 and R33 spend their visible text on rosters and mission statements without connecting the entity to any operative effect, and both are card-high. A bank that scores affiliation rather than exposure would over-credit R15/R33 and under-credit R27/R52.

proposals.name: Supplies information the agency cannot obtain elsewhere
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment contributes facts held privately by the commenter or observable only from their position: own operating or claims records, own reanalysis of a public dataset with stated method, direct field observation in the specific area or under the specific condition at issue. 5 = a mixture of privately held and already-public material. 0 = every fact in the comment is restatement of the notice, of the existing regulation, or of general knowledge already in the agency's own record. Score information novelty relative to what the agency already holds, not fact density or citation count.
proposals.rationale: R09 reanalyzes FARS with three named undercount correction factors and a dated FIRST query; R06 speaks from State Farm's own claim-handling volume and its ADAS data experience; R44 supplies American Samoa's 2013-2017 average catch of 21,139 lb against a 13,000 lb cap; R07 logs 150 days on the water with 50-plus in the exemption areas under discussion. All dense-high, card-low. By contrast R01 pastes 91.107(a)(3) back to the FAA and R05 recites the proposed regulation's own background, and both are card-high. A criterion counting facts rather than fact provenance cannot separate these.

proposals.name: Share of text that is the commenter's own, not reproduced
proposals.instruction: Estimate what fraction of the comment is the commenter's own new prose, versus quoted regulation, preamble, or notice text, versus material repeated inside the submission itself. 10 = almost all original, with quotation kept short and used to anchor a point. 5 = roughly half. 0 = the majority is verbatim regulatory or notice text, or the same letter appears twice (cover note plus attachment) with nothing added on the second pass. Count internal duplication on the reproduced side, not the original side.
proposals.rationale: R01 reproduces 91.107(a)(3) nearly whole with one sentence changed; R20 block-quotes 1.457-12(e)(2) and 1.409A-1(d) before arguing; R21 reproduces its cover note verbatim as the attached letter; R37 reproduces its email body verbatim in the attached letter. All four sit at card .805 to .986 and dense .071 to .308. Length-and-specificity criteria reward reproduced regulatory text exactly as much as authored text, which is a direct mechanism for card over-crediting this group.

proposals.name: Identifies a specific defect in the agency's analysis or instrument
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment locates a named flaw in the agency's own reasoning, data, or study design and says why it is a flaw: an unexplained design choice, an internal contradiction in the instrument, a discrepancy between preamble, rule text and forms, or a known undercount in the data the agency relied on. 5 = a flaw is gestured at but not located. 0 = the comment neither tests nor examines any part of the agency's analysis, offering only approval, disapproval, or preference. Generic complaint about the agency scores 0; the defect must be locatable in the document under comment.
proposals.rationale: R38 pins an age band of 25-54 chosen without stated rationale; R56 shows the survey asks people unlikely to have internet access to predict how they would behave with it; R36 traces a three-way disagreement among preamble, proposed rule text, and the December 2019 Form 1098-F instructions; R09 works from the GAO-identified FARS undercount. All are dense-high and card-low (card .050 to .249). A bank built from surface quality markers has no place to put this move, so it is a strong candidate for what the dense model is reading.

proposals.name: Engages the merits versus requesting only a schedule change
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment takes a position on the substance of what the agency proposed. 5 = a procedural request accompanied by real substantive comment. 0 = the comment's entire content is a request for more time or another procedural accommodation, with no position on the rule itself, however thoroughly the request is documented and footnoted. Rate the presence of merits content only; do not rate writing quality, formatting, or how well the request is justified.
proposals.rationale: R10, R21, R40 and R59 are all pure comment-period extension requests, and they carry card percentiles of .950, .986, .960 and .993 respectively against dense percentiles of .098, .308, .314 and .272. Four of the thirty card-high rows are the same procedural genre, which is the single cleanest block in the slice. These letters have everything a criterion bank tends to reward (docket number, Federal Register citations, precedent for prior extensions, named signatory) while saying nothing about the rule.

proposals.name: Net information flow: contributes to the record or draws from it
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment is overwhelmingly a contribution, putting evidence, analysis, or a defensible position into the record for the agency to use. 5 = balanced. 0 = the comment is overwhelmingly a demand on the agency: it asks the agency to explain, list, confirm, clarify, define, or supply things, without supplying anything itself. Count questions and requests for agency-produced material on the 0 side and facts, reasoning, and stated positions on the 10 side. A question that embeds the answer counts as a contribution.
proposals.rationale: R58 is page-by-page requests directed at the agency (provide a list of specific components, what proof is acceptable) and sits at dense .008, the lowest in the slice, against card .845; R55 is three bare questions with Federal Register links at dense .031 / card .656; R23 asks the IRS to confirm reliance at dense .023 / card .768. Against these, R08 and R44 put a fifty-year documentary record and territorial catch data into the record and are dense .964 and .959. Interrogative specificity looks like engagement to a criterion bank but is net extraction.

proposals.name: Written for this docket versus repurposed campaign or marketing copy
proposals.instruction: 10 = the prose is addressed to the decisionmaker in this proceeding and could not be lifted intact from another context: it names the rule, addresses the agency, and its register is that of a submission. 5 = docket-aware but partly templated. 0 = the text is evidently written for another audience and pasted in, marked by second-person consumer address, headline-style openers, action-alert urgency in the close, rhetorical questions repeated verbatim, or no addressee at all. Judge the genre of the writing only, never the position taken or the sincerity of the writer.
proposals.rationale: R04 opens 'Dads, you wouldn't knowingly bring poison into your home' and repeats its 90-ppm rhetorical question verbatim, a distributed advocacy article rather than a comment, at dense .147 / card .811; R16 closes with 'There's no time to waste. Please act swiftly', at dense .023 / card .929; R02 opens with petition language, at dense .031 / card .910. All three carry real numbers and clean prose, which is exactly why a criterion bank scores them high while the dense model does not.

proposals.name: Interest disclosed, and the argument survives the interest
proposals.instruction: 10 = the commenter's own benefit from the requested outcome is visible in the text, and the argument still rests on reasons that would hold for someone who did not get that benefit. 5 = interest visible, argument partly independent. 0 = the entire content of the argument is that the outcome would be good for the commenter, the commenter's program, or the commenter's accreditation framework, restated in public-interest language. Score disclosure and independence jointly: an undisclosed benefit driving the whole argument scores 0 even when the writing is polished.
proposals.rationale: R24 is an accreditation body urging USDA to rely on the ILAC/IAF framework of which it is a recognized member; R19 is a breeder whose income depends on the species not being listed, arguing from captive abundance; R32 and R51 are grantees urging extension of the grants that fund them. Card scores them .768, .739, .932 and .869 while dense scores .058, .116, .314 and .210. R07, by contrast, concedes that recreational fishermen should share the burden of overfishing rules before asking for the closure, and is dense .646 / card .057.

proposals.name: Engages the counterargument or concedes its own position's cost
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment states the best case against its own position, or acknowledges what its preferred outcome would cost and to whom, and then answers it. 5 = a token acknowledgment with no engagement. 0 = fully one-directional, with no tradeoff, cost, or opposing consideration acknowledged anywhere in the text. Score the presence and handling of the opposing case, not whether the commenter ends up conceding anything.
proposals.rationale: R07 writes that recreational fishermen should certainly share the burden and that he is not naive enough to think everything should be catch and release, then argues anyway; R42 grants that the proposed rule corrects several errors while still opposing it; R36 proposes an alternative Form 1098-F design and then questions whether the reporting requirement is statutorily supported at all. These are dense .646, .826 and .803 against card .057, .062 and .210. R16 and R32 are wholly one-directional and are card .929 and .932.

proposals.name: Traced causal chain from this rule to a quantified consequence
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment walks from a specific provision through named intermediate actors to a consequence with a magnitude attached, so each link can be checked. 5 = a consequence with a magnitude but no mechanism, or a mechanism with no magnitude. 0 = harm or benefit asserted at the level of a population or a value, with nothing connecting it to this particular rule. Credit the chain and its quantification; the direction of the claim is irrelevant.
proposals.rationale: R50 runs from restricting 43 million pounds through handler costs to grower price, set against 200-plus million pounds of imported product; R44 runs from a 13,000 lb cap against a 21,139 lb average catch to three to six full-time fishermen unable to subsist; R35 runs from removal of twenty varietal exemptions to a barrier to entry for imported table grapes. Dense .925, .959, .894 against card .207, .142, .105. R02 and R16 assert stakes without any chain and are card .910 and .929.

proposals.name: Accountable authorship whose stated role licenses the claims
proposals.instruction: 10 = a named person with a stated role, an organization, and reachable contact information makes claims that the stated role would actually put them in a position to know. 5 = named author whose asserted claims sit outside their stated vantage, or an organization with no individual attached. 0 = no author, no organization, and no role anywhere in the text, so nothing in it can be sourced to anyone. Score the fit between asserted role and content, not credentials or seniority.
proposals.rationale: R58 delivers detailed BSL-4 HVAC commentary with no author, organization or signature and sits at dense .008 / card .845; R55 is unattributed questions at dense .031 / card .656. Against them, R09 is a named ACUP presenter resubmitting a corrected report (dense .938) and R44 is signed by the DMWR Director as an official government response (dense .959), both card-low. Technical vocabulary is available to a criterion bank; attribution of that vocabulary to an accountable vantage is not.

proposals.name: Payload survives degraded formatting; polish without payload penalized
proposals.instruction: 10 = a clear substantive ask, claim, or fact is fully recoverable despite bad OCR, scanning artifacts, handwriting, page furniture, or ungrammatical prose. 5 = payload present but partly obscured or thin. 0 = the document is clean and well formatted but, once letterhead, roster, courtesies and restatement of the notice are removed, contains no ask, claim or fact. Explicitly ignore typography, spelling, scan quality and grammar; score only what remains when presentation is stripped away.
proposals.rationale: R22 is a garbled scanned board roster followed by a clear request that EPA continue thiamethoxam registration on behalf of 1,100 member companies (dense .989 / card .156); R50 is handwritten and OCR-mangled around an intact economic argument (dense .925 / card .207); R12 is ungrammatical but names EAJA at 28 U.S.C. 2412(d), PL 101-630, PL 93-638, H.R. 2936 section 701 and a ten-year Tule River Tribe permitting example (dense .741 / card .122). R15 and R21 are the inverse, clean and rostered with little payload, at card .873 and .986.

proposals.name: Brevity that resolves to a clear disposition from a positioned party
proposals.instruction: 10 = a short comment states an unambiguous disposition (concur, oppose, withdraw, support the adjustment, take no action) from someone whose position on that question is itself information the agency needs. 5 = a clear disposition from a party with no particular standing on it. 0 = short and non-committal, or long with the disposition never stated or buried past the point of recovery. Never penalize brevity as such; penalize only the absence of a recoverable position.
proposals.rationale: R27 is three lines from Boeing concurring with an AD on its own aircraft (dense .947 / card .177); R52 is United concurring with a fleet of twenty-one affected airplanes (dense .898 / card .173); R49, R31 and R46 are all two to four sentences with a plain position and sit at dense .726, .741 and .748 against card .018, .046 and .075. Any bank with length, structure or elaboration terms will floor these five. R15 and R05 show the inverse failure, long documents whose position is vague or arrives after pages of recitation.

proposals.name: Adversarial tone anchored in a cost the commenter actually bears
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment's sharpness, refusal, or accusation is tied to a concrete cost falling on the commenter or an identified party, and the intensity is proportionate to that cost. 5 = strong tone with a real but unquantified stake. 0 = emotional register untethered from any consequence to anyone identified, or hostility used in place of reasons. Do not reward politeness and do not penalize hostility as such; score only whether the register is earned by a borne cost.
proposals.rationale: R42 uses phrases like War on Coal and woefully misguided, but from a coal producer directly regulated by the standard, at dense .826 / card .062; R44 is a flat refusal by the government whose own waters would be closed, at dense .959 / card .142; R35 accuses a competitor committee of using the regulatory framework as a barrier to entry, at dense .894 / card .105; R50 is similar. A civility or professional-tone criterion actively inverts this group, which would explain unusually low card percentiles on otherwise substantive letters.

proposals.name: Remedy at the right grain, with a reason the agency lacks
proposals.instruction: 10 = the comment proposes a specific implementable change (a text edit, a new form field, an expanded sample frame, an added survey question, an alignment with an existing standard) AND supplies the reason for it that the agency could not have generated from its own record. 5 = a specific remedy supported only by reasoning already available to the agency, or a sound reason with no workable remedy attached. 0 = a maximal or vague ask (ban it, act swiftly, withdraw it) with neither mechanism nor supporting reason.
proposals.rationale: R36 proposes adding a box to Form 1098-F for the nondeductible amount, because penalties are always known figures while restitution and compliance amounts often are not, at dense .803 / card .210; R34 asks FDA to add survey questions on abuse-deterrent formulations, grounded in a payer's own prescribing programs, at dense .834 / card .198; R38 asks that the 25-54 age band be widened because 200 million licensed drivers range from 16 to over 90, at dense .844 / card .216; R41 asks that special conditions be aligned with the powered-lift certification basis. R16 and R02, by contrast, ask for a ban and for expanded plan options with no mechanism, at card .929 and .910.

proposals.name: Visible-text bulk and elaboration
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much running comment prose is present, judged purely by amount. 0 = the whole comment is one to three sentences or a single short paragraph; 3 = one or two substantial paragraphs; 6 = roughly a page of continuous prose; 8 = multiple pages with headings or numbered sections; 10 = many pages of dense paragraphs, still running at the point the text ends. Count words, paragraphs, sections and headings only. Do NOT judge whether the length is warranted, whether the writing is informative, or whether brevity is a virtue or a fault here. Do NOT reward or penalise the text for being long or short. Report extent only.
proposals.rationale: R02, R16, R48 and R21 are each only two or three sentences of plain prose, while R11, R42 and R31 run to multiple pages of numbered sections with footnotes. Word count is set by the submitter's drafting budget and by how many attachment pages the ingest pipeline concatenated before truncation, not by whether the point being made is correct: R02's two sentences about user-fee adjustment and R11's twelve pages on underride guards can each be sound or unsound. Any written criterion of the form 'does the comment supply supporting evidence', 'does it address multiple issues', or 'is the reasoning developed' will mechanically track bulk, so bulk has to be declared a nuisance rather than allowed to enter as a criterion.

proposals.name: Ingest-pipeline residue and transmittal stubs
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of this record consists of upload-pipeline residue rather than authored comment prose. Count: a bare integer alone on the first line (for example '1', '0', '8'); transmittal stubs such as 'See attached file(s)', 'Please see attached', 'Attached please find', 'Please accept the attached comments'; the same wording appearing twice because a short cover note was concatenated with its own attachment; pasted email-envelope headers (From:/To:/Date:/Subject:); bare page markers such as 'Page 1', 'Page 2', 'Page 2 of 8'; running heads repeating the docket number; and an abrupt cut in mid-sentence. 0 = none of these present; 5 = a stub plus some page furniture; 10 = the record is mostly such residue. Do NOT judge whether the artefacts look sloppy or professional, do NOT infer anything about the submitter from them, and do NOT let them colour any impression of the comment's content. Extent only.
proposals.rationale: R17 opens with a bare '0' followed by 'See attached file(s)'; R49 opens with a bare '8' and 'please see the attached file for comments'; R03 and R06 open on 'See attached file(s)' and '1 / See Attached'; R50's body is a pasted mail envelope ('From: tara wheeler <...>', 'To: A-AND-R-DOCKET', 'Page 1'); R13 and R54 print their substance twice because a cover note was joined to the attachment that repeats it. The leading integers are attachment counts injected during ingestion and the stubs come from the portal's cover-note field. None of this originates in the commenter's thinking, yet it consumes part of the visible window and changes how much argument a reader or a criterion ever sees.

proposals.name: OCR and scan-degradation noise
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the density of character-level corruption typical of a document that was faxed or paper-scanned and then passed through optical character recognition. Count: lookalike letter substitutions ('VVildlife' for 'Wildlife', 'ltr/ater' for 'Water', 'Ambient' rendered 'Ambient' with stray accents, 'Criterion' fused to the next word); stray spaces inside numbers and words ('(3 17) 592-46 16', 'Page2', 'August18,2017'); runs of punctuation or symbol garbage; mangled email addresses or URLs; and unreadable renderings of signatures, logos or letterhead art. 0 = clean digital text throughout; 5 = scattered corruption, a few lines affected; 10 = corruption in most lines. Judge only how much corruption is visible. Do NOT treat corruption as evidence of carelessness, low resources, age or standing, and do NOT judge whether it is good or bad.
proposals.rationale: R05 renders direct-dial numbers as '(3 17) 592-46 16' and an email as 'marc.sciscoeiGlicemiller.com'; R10 has 'ltr/ater Quality', 'Criterion' fused to a following word, 'V/orks' and 'Inigated'; R40 prints 'VVildEarth' and 'VVildlife' throughout; R28 opens on a line of symbol garbage; R57 ends in an unreadable signature scrawl; R58 has whole board-roster lines destroyed. The corruption is produced by the route the paper travelled and by the docket's own imaging, not by the commenter's reasoning, and it appears on both sides of this slice (R05, R10, R28, R40 alongside R57, R58). It nevertheless makes a document read as either garbled or crisp, and both a text-reading model and any keyword-matching criterion will respond to that.
proposals.upstream_parent: document-production and submission medium (fax or paper scan versus a native electronic file)

proposals.name: Letterhead furniture and signature credentialing
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the visible text is occupied by professional correspondence furniture surrounding the argument, rather than by argument. Count: printed letterhead with street address, suite, city and ZIP; telephone, direct-dial, fax and website lines; blocks such as 'WRITER'S DIRECT NUMBER' / 'DIRECT FAX' / 'INTERNET'; submission-route lines ('VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION', 'Submitted via www.regulations.gov', 'VIA Facsimile'); formal RE: / Subject: blocks and repeated running heads; officer or board rosters; and closing signature blocks carrying a personal name plus rank or credential (Ph.D., MPH, 'Vice President, Regulatory Affairs', 'Senior Director', 'Executive Director', 'Designated Engineering Representative'). 0 = no such furniture at all; 5 = a standard address block plus a titled signature; 10 = the furniture fills most of the visible text. Do NOT judge whether the furniture looks impressive, official or legitimate, and do NOT infer competence, seniority or seriousness from it. Extent only.
proposals.rationale: R05 spends its entire first page on Ice Miller letterhead - three separate direct-number / fax / internet triplets and two full IRS mailing addresses - before any argument appears; R58 spends the whole visible window on a Georgia Agribusiness Council board-of-directors roster giving company and town for some forty names; R01 carries a footer with street, suite, phone and fax; R13, R24, R32 and R59 close with a name plus rank ('Sanjay Gummalla, Ph.D., Vice President, Scientific and Regulatory Affairs'; 'Ali Bahrami, Vice President, Civil Aviation'), while R21 and R38 have no such block at all. This furniture is a fingerprint of possessing an office, a letterhead template and a titled signatory - an upstream resource and seniority story that leaves a very visible trace - and it also competes directly with argument for the limited visible window. Tagged mixed because a well-staffed regulatory-affairs shop may also genuinely produce stronger analysis, so the discount should be reported as a band.
proposals.upstream_parent: institutional resources and author seniority (a staffed office with letterhead, a mailroom and titled signatories)

proposals.name: Organizational self-credentialing by scale
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much text is spent describing the submitting organization and quantifying its size, reach, tenure or standing, as opposed to discussing the rule. Count sentences stating member or employee counts, premium or revenue figures, market share, number of accredited or served entities, years in operation, geographic footprint, founding date, or a mission statement - for example 'more than 1,500 member companies', 'annual premiums of $323 billion', '67 percent of homeowners', 'workforce of 225,000 people', 'more than 1.7 million members and online activists', 'over 3700 actively accredited organizations', 'has served public pension plans for more than 25 years'. 0 = no self-description; 3 = a single identifying clause; 5 = one full self-description paragraph; 10 = several paragraphs, or self-description occupying most of the visible text. Do NOT judge whether the organization sounds important, credible or well qualified to comment, and do NOT let claimed scale affect any other impression. Extent only.
proposals.rationale: R18 gives a full paragraph to 'more than 1,500 member companies ... $323 billion in annual premiums ... 67 percent of homeowners, 55 percent of automobile'; R53 to 'our workforce of 225,000 people serves the health care needs of more than 125 million people worldwide'; R33 to 'more than 1.7 million members and online activists'; R51 to 'over 3700 actively accredited organizations ... over five hundred food testing laboratories'; R01 and R03 open on comparable self-portraits. These sentences describe the sender, not the rule - they are a bid for standing, and they are exactly the kind of claim a written criterion about 'demonstrated expertise' or 'relevant standing' would reward. Tagged mixed because a large membership can also mean genuinely better field information, so both the discounted and undiscounted readouts are needed.
proposals.upstream_parent: institutional standing and reputational capital of the submitting organization

proposals.name: Personalized addressing of a named agency official
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how personally the text addresses a specific human being at the agency. 0 = no addressee, or a wholly generic one ('To Whom It May Concern', 'Dear Sir or Madam', 'Dear Sir/Madam', 'Dear Sirs', 'Dear Friends', or address to a docket clerk, mail code or docket number only). 4 = a named official addressed by title and surname ('Dear Secretary Perdue', 'Dear Ms. Jennings', 'Dear Administrator Wheeler', 'Dear Acting Administrator Carlson'). 7 = the named official's exact office, division, branch or mail code is reproduced ('Ms. Kirsten Wielobob, Deputy Commissioner for Services and Enforcement'; 'Jeffrey Waite, Chief, Audit Services Branch, Quality Assessment Division'). 10 = first-name or familiar address, or explicit reference to prior direct contact with that person or office. Do NOT judge whether such familiarity is appropriate, impressive, presumptuous or improper, and do NOT infer anything about the quality of what follows the salutation. Extent only.
proposals.rationale: R34 opens 'Dear Gam,' and R54 opens 'Dear Brian;' - first-name address to the responsible official; R09 opens 'Talofa Mike,' and refers to prior correspondence from that office; R42 notes 'I appreciate the opportunity to present at the ACUP meeting'; R04 addresses 'Ms. Kirsten Wielobob, Deputy Commissioner for Services and Enforcement' and R51 'Jeffrey Waite, Chief, Audit Services Branch' by exact office. By contrast R01, R29 and R17 write 'Dear Sir or Madam' / 'Dear Sir/Madam' and R21 writes 'To Wom It May Concern'. Knowing an official's name - still more, their first name - is a fingerprint of prior contact and network position, which sits entirely upstream of the text. Tagged mixed because someone who has worked a docket before may also understand it better.
proposals.upstream_parent: the author's network and access to agency staff - knowing who handles this docket, and how well

proposals.name: Ritual deference boilerplate and reused house template
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the density of stock courtesy formulas and interchangeable template scaffolding - wording that would sit unchanged in a letter to any agency about any rule. Count phrases such as 'appreciates the opportunity to comment', 'welcomes the opportunity to respond to this request for comments', 'respectfully submits', 'Thank you for your consideration', 'Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions', 'we look forward to working with the agency'; also count passages that simply restate the Federal Register notice's own summary of what the agency proposes, and any paragraph that reads as a fixed block carried between submissions. 0 = none of these; 5 = the usual opening and closing formulas plus some restatement; 10 = the visible text is almost entirely formulas and restatement of the notice. Do NOT judge whether the courtesy is sincere, whether template reuse is lazy or efficient, or whether the boilerplate is well written. Extent only.
proposals.rationale: R18, R43 and R44 are three National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies letters sharing an identical opening line ('Please accept this comment from the National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies.'), an identical membership paragraph and an identical 'welcomes the opportunity to respond to this request for comments', with only the docket, date and administrator's name swapped, and each then paraphrases the notice back to the agency for a paragraph or two; R24, R32 and R13 close on near-identical 'Please do not hesitate to contact me ... Thank you for your consideration'; R03, R31, R47, R51 and R60 all open on 'appreciates' or 'welcomes the opportunity'. What such phrases measure is the existence of the template, not anything about this comment - they are constant across submissions that differ wildly in what they actually say.
proposals.upstream_parent: a regulatory-affairs office reusing a standing letter template across dockets

proposals.name: Citation apparatus and footnote scaffolding
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the density of formal citation machinery visible in the text. Count: pin cites to the Federal Register, U.S. Code, CFR or Treasury regulations ('83 Fed. Reg. 56,763', '16 U.S.C. 1539(j)(2)(A)', '26 CFR 1.6050X-1(e)', 'Treas. Reg. 1.6049-5(c)(5)', '85 FR 28524'); numbered or superscript footnotes with their own reference lines; 'Id.' and short-form cites; quoted defined terms introduced parenthetically; and hyperlinked or bracketed sources with an 'as of' or 'last accessed' date. 0 = no citations of any kind; 5 = a handful of statutory or Federal Register references; 10 = citations or footnotes attached to nearly every assertion. Count the apparatus only. Do NOT check whether the citations are accurate, apt or load-bearing, do NOT follow or verify them, and do NOT treat their presence or absence as evidence of rigour or its lack.
proposals.rationale: R33 pin-cites '16 U.S.C. 1539(j)(2)(A)' and '87 Fed. Reg 34625' with numbered footnotes; R47 cites '83 Fed. Reg. 56,763' and 'section 1.401(k)-1(d)(3)(v)(B)'; R20 works through 'Treas. Reg. 1.6049-5(c)(5)' with a full defined-term apparatus; R11 runs seven footnotes across two pages; R25 footnotes an academic paper with a URL and an access date; R30 cites '85 FR 28533' and 'Proposed 26 CFR 1.6050X-1(e)'. Footnote scaffolding is what a legal drafting shop produces by habit, and it appears on both sides of this slice, so it indexes the drafting pipeline behind the letter rather than the merit of the position argued. Tagged mixed because counsel-drafted comments may also be substantively stronger, so the discount belongs in a sensitivity band.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional legal drafting - retained outside counsel or an in-house legal department preparing the filing

proposals.name: Procedural scheduling ask rather than position on the rule
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the operative request in the text is an administrative or scheduling accommodation rather than a statement about what the rule should say. 10 = the entire submission asks for process relief - a comment-period extension, a deadline change, a reopening, or withdrawal and replacement of a prior filing - and states no position on the rule's content ('respectfully requests a 30-day extension of the comment period'; 'we respectfully request FDA extend its comment period for this ANPRM by 90 days'; 'requests that the comment previously submitted ... be deleted from the record and replaced'). 5 = a process request and a substantive position both appear. 0 = the text is entirely about the content of the rule and asks for no process relief. Do NOT judge whether the process request is reasonable, well justified or worth granting, and do NOT treat the presence or absence of a substantive position as a merit or a defect. Extent only.
proposals.rationale: R13 (American Frozen Food Institute), R24 (Consumer Brands Association), R28 (Al Fakher Tobacco) and R32 (American Chemistry Council Center for Biocide Chemistries) are all pure comment-period-extension requests: each carries a complete formal letter, a docket RE: line, a credentialed signature and a courteous close, and the only operative ask is more time; R06 additionally asks that a prior submission 'be deleted from the record and replaced in its entirety'. The genre is produced by a calendar-monitoring workflow rather than by having something to say about the rule, and its textual fingerprint - a fully furnished letter whose ask is procedural - is exactly what makes it look complete against any criterion bank scoring form, clarity of request, or specificity of the relief sought.
proposals.upstream_parent: an association's routine docket-monitoring and calendar-management workflow (a filing is generated because a deadline is near, not because the member has an analysis ready)

proposals.name: Alphanumeric identifier density (parts, models, sections, standards)
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the visible text consists of codified identifier strings rather than ordinary sentences. Count: part and model numbers ('P/N MA30A1017'; 'V2522-A5, V2524-A5, V2527-A5, V2527E-A5'); service-bulletin, directive and NPRM numbers ('SB 777-28A0034 Rev. 3'; 'NPRM 2015-NM-169-AD'; 'NMSB V2500-ENG-72-0671'); consensus-standard designations ('ASTM E1527-21'; 'ISO/IEC 17025'); statutory and regulatory subsection strings ('1.457-12(e)(2)(i)'; 'section 1.401(k)-1(d)(3)(v)(B)'; 'section 958(b)(4)'); form, file and program codes ('Form 1098-F'; 'CMS-1672-P'; 'CFDA number 84.382A'); and docket, RIN and mail-code strings. 0 = essentially none; 5 = identifiers appear regularly but sentences dominate; 10 = identifier strings outnumber ordinary words. Do NOT judge whether the identifiers are used correctly, whether they signal expertise, or whether the subject matter is important. Count them only.
proposals.rationale: R54 is largely a list of engine model designations plus a service-bulletin number; R15 turns entirely on 'P/N MA30A1017' and 'Boeing SB 777-28A0034 Rev. 3'; R05 and R47 are dense with subsection strings such as '1.457-12(e)(2)(i)' and 'section 1.401(k)-1(d)(3)(v)(B)'; R06 turns on 'ASTM E1527-21' versus 'E1527-13'; R59 works through numbered Special Conditions; while R21, R35, R48 and R55 contain almost no identifiers at all. Identifier density is a property of which regulatory instrument the docket concerns - some dockets simply are about part numbers and code subsections - so it is a topic fingerprint that travels with the agency and the rule type rather than with how good the comment is. Any criterion rewarding specificity, technical precision or 'cites the exact provision at issue' will pick identifier density up automatically, which is why it must be declared and discounted rather than admitted to the bank.

proposals.name: Substantive engagement with rule vs. procedural-only content
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 how much of the comment engages with the actual substance/merits of the proposed action (specific provisions, its rationale, its effects) as opposed to addressing only a procedural/administrative matter such as requesting a filing extension or serving as a bare transmittal note. A 10 is a comment entirely devoted to arguing about what the rule does and whether/how it should change. A 0 is a comment whose entire content is procedural housekeeping (e.g., 'please extend the comment period by 30 days') with no engagement with the rule's substance.
proposals.rationale: Extension-request letters R04, R14, R16, and R45 are near-identical in structure (formal ask for more time, no position on the rule's merits) and all sit at dense_low/card_high (dense .27-.31, card .95-.99). By contrast R01 and R38 are dense_high/card_low (dense .92/.83) and are built entirely around substantive analysis of what the collection/rule does. The scorecard appears to reward professional letter form regardless of whether the letter says anything about the rule, while the dense model discounts pure procedural asks.

proposals.name: States concrete real-world stakes of the decision
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment specifies who is affected and how (magnitude of harm/benefit, populations, consequences of the decision) rather than treating the matter as an abstract or narrow point with no stated real-world consequence. 10 = concrete stakes clearly stated (numbers of people/animals/dollars affected, type of harm). 0 = no stakes or consequence stated anywhere in the comment.
proposals.rationale: R17 (side underride guards) states 5,700 deaths and a 71% increase since 2009, and R08 (bottomfish) gives specific subsistence catch figures; both are dense_high (.964, .959) with card_low. R40 and R44, narrow engine-model-number corrections, state no consequence of the discrepancy at all and are dense_low (.129, .075) despite card_high (.985, .909).

proposals.name: Personal/institutional stake paired with first-hand specific detail
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter BOTH (a) has an evident direct personal or organizational stake in the outcome AND (b) grounds that stake in concrete first-hand detail (specific numbers, places, roles, experiences) rather than only reciting third-party statistics. 10 = both a clear personal/institutional stake and first-hand concrete grounding are present. 0 = neither is present -- no stated stake and no first-hand detail, only generic or borrowed facts.
proposals.rationale: R28 (charter captain, 150 days on the water, names specific fishing spots 'McBlair's and Old South Rips') and R08 (territorial government agency citing its own catch data, 2013-2017 average 21,139 lb) are dense_high (.646, .959)/card_low. R03, which cites only third-party NOAA/aggregate statistics with a generic 'I support' framing and no stated personal stake, is dense_low (.023)/card_high (.929).

proposals.name: Authentic, non-templated individual voice
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the language reads as an individually composed statement -- including imperfect, digressive, or idiosyncratic phrasing -- rather than reusable advocacy-campaign boilerplate that could be dropped unchanged into many different submitters' comments. 10 = clearly idiosyncratic, personally composed language, even if unpolished or off-topic in places. 0 = generic, interchangeable advocacy phrasing typical of an action-alert template.
proposals.rationale: R25 rambles personally into the commenter's own views on nuclear energy and is dense_high (.654)/card_low (.030). R07 ('This is very important to support my needs and religious freedom... I applaud... I encourage... I urge') and R03 ('I respectfully ask... I support an immediate ban...') read as generic template language and are both dense_low (.031, .023)/card_high (.910, .929).

proposals.name: Holds the agency accountable to its own stated rationale or history
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment specifically interrogates the agency's own stated reasoning, history, or prior representations -- pointing out an unexplained choice, an inconsistency, or an unfulfilled past commitment -- rather than simply stating the commenter's own preference in isolation. 10 = comment identifies a specific gap or inconsistency in the agency's own reasoning/track record and argues from it. 0 = comment states a position with no reference to the agency's own reasoning or history.
proposals.rationale: R02 specifically flags that NHTSA gave 'no justification' for restricting its study to ages 25-54; R17 notes DOT acknowledged the underride risk in 1969 but 'TSC is unaware of DOT completing a single' study in 54 years. Both are dense_high (.844, .964)/card_low. R07 simply states a preference with no engagement with the agency's own reasoning and is dense_low (.031)/card_high (.910).

proposals.name: Explicit causal chain from fact to recommended consequence
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explicitly connects a specific factual claim to a specific consequence for the decision via a stated causal or logical mechanism, rather than listing facts, questions, or citations without tying them into an argument. 10 = a clear 'because X, therefore Y should happen' chain is spelled out. 0 = facts or questions are listed with no connecting logic to a recommendation.
proposals.rationale: R23 explicitly reasons that because neonicotinoids are 'highly water soluble' they 'travel in soil, water' and therefore 'should be regulated' -- dense .748/card .075. R20, by contrast, is a list of unanswered process questions with no connecting argument to a recommendation, and is dense_low (.031)/card_high (.656).

proposals.name: Decisive, unambiguous stated position
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment takes a clear, unambiguous stance (support, oppose, or a specific requested change) rather than only posing open questions or expressing unresolved uncertainty. 10 = an unambiguous position is stated. 0 = the comment consists entirely of questions or non-committal musing with no stated position.
proposals.rationale: R21 ('We urge National Marine Fisheries to take NO action... keeping the habitat management area CLOSED') and R13 (clear endorsement of the carrot-grading proposal with a stated reason) are both dense_high (.871, .741)/card_low. R20 is entirely a list of unanswered questions with no position taken, and is dense_low (.031)/card_high (.656).

proposals.name: Demonstrates command of the rule's broader purpose and context
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment situates its point within an account of what the overall regulatory action does, why, and how this piece fits the whole, rather than raising an isolated point in a contextual vacuum. 10 = comment clearly explains the broader program/rule and its purpose before or alongside making its point. 0 = comment raises a narrow point with no surrounding explanation of what the broader rule/program is or does.
proposals.rationale: R01 explains the IIJA Section 24108(d) grant program and its purpose before addressing the specific information collection; R15 explains what the NPRM mandates and for how many aircraft. Both are dense_high (.924, .898)/card_low. R40 and R44 are bare part-number corrections with no explanation of the broader AD's purpose, and are dense_low (.129, .075)/card_high (.985, .909).

proposals.name: Acknowledges trade-offs while still reaching a clear bottom line
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment BOTH acknowledges some complexity, competing interest, or limit of its own position AND still reaches a clear overall recommendation. 10 = genuine nuance/trade-off acknowledgment is present alongside a clear conclusion. 0 = the comment is entirely one-sided with no acknowledgment of any competing consideration, OR is so hedged it never reaches a conclusion.
proposals.rationale: R28 explicitly weighs recreational vs. commercial fishing interests ('I am not naive enough to think we should be all catch and release, but...') while still reaching a clear recommendation against opening the exemption areas; dense .646/card .057. R07 is entirely one-sided advocacy with no acknowledgment of any competing consideration, dense .031/card .910.

proposals.name: Discloses sources, methods, and uncertainty behind cited figures
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether, when the comment relies on numbers or estimates, it discloses where they came from and their limitations (e.g., naming multiple competing estimates, flagging known undercounts, correcting its own prior errors) rather than presenting figures as bare, unsourced assertions. 10 = sources/methods and their uncertainty are made explicit. 0 = numeric claims are stated with no indication of source or method.
proposals.rationale: R43 names three different named sources for competing 'undercount correction factors' (1.77, 2.4, 3.1) and explicitly notes it is correcting a typo from its own prior submission -- dense .938/card .249. By contrast R09 asserts a precise figure ('$1 billion... in 2019 alone') with no stated source or method, and is dense_low (.123) despite being card_high (.787).

proposals.name: Concrete actionable ask paired with an explained consequence
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment BOTH gives a specific, concrete ask (a number, a provision, a wording change) AND explains why that specific change matters in practical/administrative/real-world terms. 10 = both a specific ask and a stated reason it matters are present. 0 = the comment gives no concrete ask, OR gives one with no explanation of why it matters.
proposals.rationale: R53 asks for a specific $50,000 reporting threshold and explains it avoids 'major administrative burden'; dense .803/card .210. R06 (AAMVA) asks for removal of 'duplicative grant application and processing requirements' and explains this lets programs focus on 'delivery of public benefit'; dense .712/card .136. R40/R44 give a specific ask (remove certain engine models from an applicability list) with no stated consequence of getting it wrong, and are dense_low (.129, .075)/card_high.

proposals.name: Stated expertise is used to generate a specific insight, not just asserted
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter's stated credential, role, or experience is actually put to work to produce a specific, non-obvious technical judgment, rather than the credential being asserted while the rest of the comment stays at the level of generic support or opposition. 10 = credential is stated and clearly generates a specific technical point a lay commenter could not have made. 0 = a credential/affiliation is stated but the substantive content that follows is generic and could have been written by anyone.
proposals.rationale: R08's Director of AS-DMWR uses his position to produce a specific jurisdictional argument (federal-water closures alone won't reduce nearshore catch) and specific comparative catch data; dense .959/card .142. R43 uses stated methodological expertise to interrogate FARS undercounting with named correction factors; dense .938/card .249. By contrast R54 opens with extensive credentials (accredited since 1979, ISO/IEC 17025 competence) but the visible argument mainly restates a preference for an existing framework without a comparably distinct technical insight, and is dense_low (.023) despite card_high (.768).

proposals.name: Vivid, concrete narrative or sensory grounding of impact
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment uses vivid, concrete narrative or sensory detail (specific places, scenes, cultural or personal texture) that makes the described impact tangible, as opposed to remaining entirely at the level of abstract policy language. 10 = comment includes vivid, specific narrative/sensory detail. 0 = comment is written entirely in abstract, generic policy language with no scene-setting or texture.
proposals.rationale: R28 names specific fishing grounds and describes the commenter's own days on the water; R08 invokes specific cultural terms ('fa'asamoa,' 'fa'alavelave') tying the fishery to lived practice. Both are dense_high (.646, .959)/card_low. R59, a policy letter about HRA safe harbors, stays entirely in abstract regulatory language with no narrative texture and is dense_low (.091) despite card_high (.888).

proposals.name: Directly organized around the agency's own enumerated questions
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment is structured to directly answer specific questions or numbered items that the agency's own notice asked for comment on, rather than offering a free-form reaction organized around the commenter's own self-chosen themes. 10 = comment is explicitly numbered/organized to track the agency's own request-for-comment structure. 0 = comment does not engage with or reference any specific question the notice posed.
proposals.rationale: R30 (AbbVie) explicitly numbers its response to match the notice's own enumerated questions ('1. Whether the proposed collection of information is necessary... 3. Ways to enhance the quality...'); dense .887/card .130. R56 (Covered California) instead organizes around its own self-chosen headings ('Mitigating the Risk of Choice Overload') rather than the agency's specific numbered questions, and is dense_low (.183) despite card_high (.842).

proposals.name: Concrete practical cost/burden/benefit analysis, not just a normative stance
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment analyzes the practical, administrative, or financial burden or benefit of the proposed action in concrete terms (operational impact, cost, resource implications) rather than only asserting a normative position (support/oppose) with no such analysis. 10 = concrete burden/benefit analysis is provided. 0 = comment asserts a position with no analysis of practical costs, burdens, or benefits.
proposals.rationale: R06 (AAMVA) analyzes how 'duplicative grant application and processing requirements' burden states and argues flexibility would let funds go to 'delivery of public benefit'; dense .712/card .136. R55 (Eversheds Sutherland) works through the practical RVO/RIN mechanics of how the rule would operate for specific fuel categories; dense .979/card .405. R45, an extension-request letter, contains no burden/benefit analysis of the underlying rule at all, and is dense_low (.314) despite card_high (.960).

proposals.name: Overall length and verbosity of the submission
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (extremely terse, a sentence or two) to 10 (very long, multi-page with extensive elaboration), rate how much text volume this comment contains. Score the sheer AMOUNT of text present, not whether the length is appropriate or whether the content in it is good.
proposals.rationale: Terse one-line concurrences (R03: 'Concur, no additional comments will be forthcoming' -- dense_pct=.947, card_pct=.177) sit at the opposite length extreme from long multi-page letters with extensive elaboration and footnotes (R05: multi-page Covered California letter -- dense_pct=.183, card_pct=.842). Because the scorecard aggregates many separately-scored criteria, longer text simply has more surface area to accumulate points, independent of whether the underlying position is sound.

proposals.name: Use of a generic 'see attached' portal-textbox opener
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (the comment opens directly with substantive content) to 10 (the comment opens with a generic placeholder phrase like 'See attached file(s)' or 'Please see attached' before any substantive content appears), rate how much of the item's opening consists of this kind of generic placeholder text. Do not judge whether using an attachment was a good choice.
proposals.rationale: R08 (Al Fakher Tobacco Factory letter) and R30 (NYC Brownfield Partnership letter) both open with a bare placeholder line ('See attached file(s)' / 'See Attached') before the real letter text begins, an artifact of how the submission portal splits a short web-form textbox from an uploaded PDF attachment. Both land dense_low_card_high (R08: dense=.098/card=.950; R30: dense=.058/card=.834), suggesting the scorecard does not penalize, and may even be inflated by, this pure interface artifact.

proposals.name: Density of OCR/scan garbling and corrupted characters
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (clean, normally rendered text throughout) to 10 (text is heavily interspersed with garbled character sequences, broken ligatures, or nonsense symbol strings characteristic of poor OCR/scan conversion), rate how much of the text shows this kind of character-level corruption. Do not judge whether the underlying argument is good.
proposals.rationale: R08 (Al Fakher Tobacco Factory, e.g. 't·r·r- ~l.att e:!*U ~Lilt t-• itO 4') and R31 (Calleguas Creek Stakeholders, e.g. 'ltr/ater Quality Standards', 'Woter Quality Criterionþr') both show heavy character-level OCR garbling from scanned/faxed originals, and both land dense_low_card_high (R08: dense=.098/card=.950; R31: dense=.153/card=.873) -- a pure artifact of the document-capture pipeline, unrelated to the argument's merit.

proposals.name: Density of numbered footnote or endnote markers
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (no footnote/endnote markers anywhere) to 10 (frequent superscript or bracketed footnote numbers throughout, each tied to a citation), rate how much the text uses this footnoting convention. Do not judge whether the cited sources are actually relevant or correct.
proposals.rationale: R05 (Covered California) carries three numbered footnotes citing an academic paper and prior Federal Register notices, and R21 (Consumer Brands Association) carries a numbered footnote citing '88 FR 7315'; both land dense_low_card_high (R05: dense=.183/card=.842; R21: dense=.272/card=.993), suggesting the scorecard rewards the mere presence of the footnoting convention rather than the underlying argument.

proposals.name: Precision/completeness of docket, RIN, or CFR citation strings
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (no formal docket number, RIN, or CFR section is cited) to 10 (a fully formed, precisely formatted regulatory citation string is present -- e.g. an exact Docket No., RIN number, or CFR section cite), rate how complete and precisely formatted such citation strings are. Do not judge whether the comment's position on the rule is correct.
proposals.rationale: R33 (International Aero Engines) cites an exact 'Docket Number FAA-2016-7099' plus a precisely dated internal service-bulletin reference, and R05 (Covered California) cites 'RIN 0938-AU97' and 'CMS-9899-P'; both land dense_low_card_high (R33: dense=.129/card=.985; R05: dense=.183/card=.842) near the very top of the card-percentile range, suggesting the scorecard may reward citation-string formatting as a proxy for rigor.

proposals.name: Recitation of the submitter organization's size or market share
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (no mention of the submitting organization's membership count, revenue, or market share) to 10 (the text prominently recites such statistics, e.g. member counts, dollar figures, or percentage market share), rate how much of the text is devoted to this kind of self-credentialing. Do not judge whether the organization's scale is actually relevant to its argument.
proposals.rationale: (a) A well-resourced trade association can devote more staff time to producing a comment and also has an incentive to remind the reader of its scale/legitimacy. (b) That incentive leaves a visible textual fingerprint: a stock paragraph reciting membership counts and market statistics. (c) R07 (NAMIC: '1,500 member companies... $323 billion in annual premiums... 67 percent of homeowners...') and R13 (State Farm: '40 million active automobile insurance policies... 19,400 agents... 53,000 employees') both open with this credential recitation and both land dense_high_card_low (R07: dense=.924/card=.050; R13: dense=.835/card=.086), consistent with the dense model being swayed by apparent institutional authority independent of argument content. Tagged mixed because a genuinely larger, better-resourced organization may also produce genuinely more substantive comments, so this factor could be doing double duty.

proposals.name: Presence of law-firm/counsel-style drafting conventions
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (no law-firm/professional-counsel drafting conventions present) to 10 (heavy use of such conventions -- e.g. multiple named attorneys with individual direct-dial phone/fax lines, a formal 'Re:' citation block, or a salutation like 'Ladies and Gentlemen:'), rate how much the text exhibits this drafting style. Do not judge whether the legal analysis itself is correct.
proposals.rationale: (a) A commenter who can afford outside counsel or an in-house tax/legal department to draft the letter differs systematically from one who writes it themselves. (b) That difference leaves a fingerprint: multiple attorney signature blocks with direct-dial numbers, formal 'Re:' blocks, and stock legal salutations. (c) R40 (Ice Miller LLP, three attorneys each with individual direct-dial and fax numbers, 'Ladies and Gentlemen:') and R29 (Prudential Financial's in-house Tax Department, formal 'Re: REG-104223-18' block) both exhibit this apparatus and both land dense_low_card_high (R40: dense=.071/card=.805; R29: dense=.229/card=.899). Tagged mixed because professionally drafted comments may also genuinely be better argued, not merely better dressed.

proposals.name: Extent of purely administrative content with no rule-merits position
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (the entire comment addresses the substance/merits of the proposed rule) to 10 (the comment is entirely or almost entirely a procedural, administrative act -- e.g. a request to extend the comment deadline, or a bare 'we concur/have no further comments' statement -- with no position taken on the rule's merits), rate how much of the text is this kind of administrative-only content. Do not judge whether making that procedural request was a reasonable thing to do.
proposals.rationale: (a) Whether a submission is a deadline-extension request or a rubber-stamp concurrence is a function of the producer's internal review timeline and workflow, not the merits of the rule. (b) That process leaves a fingerprint: the entire text is procedural boilerplate rather than substantive engagement with the rule's text. (c) R01 (ACC/CBC: 'requests a 30-day extension of the comment period... to allow appropriate experts [to] review') and R03 (Boeing: 'Concur, no additional comments will be forthcoming') are both purely administrative with zero rule-merits content, yet land in OPPOSITE quadrants (R01: dense=.314/card=.960, dense_low_card_high; R03: dense=.947/card=.177, dense_high_card_low) -- showing the two models react to the same non-substantive administrative pattern in opposite directions, evidence this factor drives disagreement rather than tracking genuine quality. Tagged mixed because a fast, confident 'no further comments' can also reflect that the organization's concerns were already genuinely satisfied -- a legitimately appropriate response, not just an artifact.

proposals.name: Signatory's seniority title paired with a direct personal contact line
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (no named signatory, or a signatory with no title/direct contact info given) to 10 (the letter closes with a named signatory carrying a senior title -- e.g. Executive Director, Vice President, Senior Manager -- plus a direct personal phone/fax/email), rate how much of this signature-block signaling is present. Do not judge whether the signatory's seniority makes their argument more correct.
proposals.rationale: (a) More senior staff are more likely to personally sign a comment on a politically or commercially important docket, and their offices are more likely to list direct contact lines. (b) That seniority leaves a fingerprint in the signature block: title plus direct phone/fax. (c) R03 (Boeing: 'Erica Graham, Senior Manager, Airplane Safety Engineering' with direct phone (425) 239-3247 and fax) and R10 (AIA: 'Ali Bahrami, Vice President, Civil Aviation') both carry this senior-title-plus-direct-contact signature, yet land in different quadrants (R03 dense_high_card_low dense=.947/card=.177; R10 dense_low_card_high dense=.173/card=.957), again suggesting this is a cross-cutting fingerprint rather than a marker of genuine substance. Tagged mixed because more senior signatories may also, on average, bring genuinely more authoritative technical input.

proposals.name: Stock rhetorical phrasing typical of an advocacy-campaign template
proposals.instruction: On a scale of 0 (phrasing reads as the commenter's own individually composed words) to 10 (phrasing follows a recognizable mass-mailer/advocacy-campaign formula -- e.g. a direct rhetorical address like 'Dear Friends,'/'Dads, you wouldn't...', or a stock urgent-appeal formula like 'I respectfully ask/urge/support...'), rate how much the text reads as templated campaign copy rather than an individually composed statement. Do not judge whether the position being urged is correct.
proposals.rationale: (a) Advocacy organizations (e.g. environmental or health NGOs) commonly supply supporters with template language to submit as their own comment, a mobilization effort entirely upstream of the individual submitter's own reasoning. (b) That mobilization leaves a fingerprint: recognizable rhetorical-appeal formulas repeated across submitters. (c) R06 ('I respectfully ask that you please help protect the Banggai Cardinalfish. I support an immediate ban...') and R15 (Earthjustice: 'Dads, you wouldn't knowingly bring poison into your home...') both show this campaign-template phrasing and both land dense_low_card_high (R06: dense=.023/card=.929; R15: dense=.147/card=.811). Because agencies conventionally discount duplicate/templated comments as not contributing unique substantive content, this factor is tagged as a purer nuisance rather than mixed with genuine quality.

proposals.name: Firsthand operational grounding
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter describes direct, relevant experience with the affected activity, system, population, or conditions; score 0 when no relevant firsthand or operational knowledge is provided.
proposals.rationale: R48 reports 150 days fishing in the affected areas, while R40 describes Louisiana’s EMS system, providers, practitioners, and ambulance constraints.

proposals.name: Empirical specificity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when claims are anchored in multiple concrete figures, measurements, dates, studies, or observed facts; score 0 when claims are wholly general or unsupported.
proposals.rationale: R24 supplies crash, fatality, injury, and economic-loss statistics, while R56 explains datasets, years, and correction factors used for its estimates.

proposals.name: Traceable evidence use
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when evidence is tied to identifiable studies, agencies, records, standards, or cited source material that directly supports the argument; score 0 when sources are absent, vague, or merely invoked rhetorically.
proposals.rationale: R24 cites NHTSA, IIHS, BLS, and specific reports, while R49 identifies Wuebbles and multiple scientific sources in addressing species threats.

proposals.name: Mechanistic causal reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment clearly explains how the proposed policy would produce specific intermediate effects and consequences; score 0 when it states only approval, opposition, or an unelaborated prediction.
proposals.rationale: R19 explains how retaining two standards could produce inadequate historical research and brownfield stigma, while R36 traces equipment or power failures to airflow reversal and containment risks.

proposals.name: Actionable textual remedy
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes precise replacement language, applicability limits, procedures, thresholds, or form changes that could be implemented directly; score 0 when it offers no concrete remedy beyond support or opposition.
proposals.rationale: R11 supplies replacement language for an FAA requirement, while R59 proposes explicit treatment of unknown amounts and specific form fields.

proposals.name: System-interaction analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment analyzes interactions among agencies, programs, standards, markets, or operational components and explains why coordination matters; score 0 when it treats the proposal in isolation.
proposals.rationale: R01 distinguishes federal and territorial waters and their different effects, while R32 analyzes coordination between renewable-fuel and vehicle-emissions programs.

proposals.name: Feasible alternative pathway
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter offers a realistic alternative, pilot, exemption, phase-in, funding mechanism, or safeguard that addresses the stated problem; score 0 when no alternative path is offered.
proposals.rationale: R22 proposes a general rule with an exemption mechanism for unusual rotorcraft circumstances, while R23 recommends native-range conservation first and carefully limited outside-range experimentation.

proposals.name: Issue prioritization
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment separates central objections or recommendations from secondary points and directs attention to the most consequential issues; score 0 when it is undifferentiated, diffuse, or limited to a single unexplained position.
proposals.rationale: R09 organizes concerns into three distinct transition issues, while R40 presents three separately prioritized ambulance-safety funding needs.

proposals.name: Representativeness assessment
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment examines whether data, samples, categories, or affected groups adequately represent relevant populations and identifies concrete coverage gaps; score 0 when representativeness is not considered.
proposals.rationale: R33 challenges an age range as unrepresentative of U.S. drivers, while R34 discusses sampling, segmentation, and the relationship between target populations and research design.

proposals.name: Boundary-condition awareness
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter identifies uncertainty, exceptions, limiting conditions, or contexts in which the proposed reasoning may not apply; score 0 when claims are absolute and unqualified.
proposals.rationale: R36 distinguishes sustained from instantaneous airflow reversal and different containment settings, while R60 distinguishes domestic captive populations from conditions in the species’ native environment.

proposals.name: Distributional impact analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment connects the proposal to concrete effects on identifiable communities, users, regions, or vulnerable groups and explains the distribution of those effects; score 0 when affected parties are mentioned only abstractly.
proposals.rationale: R14 discusses rural seniors, home-health agencies, patients, and reimbursement differences, while R01 connects fishing restrictions to American Samoa’s subsistence, livelihood, and cultural practices.

proposals.name: Temporal and comparative context
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses historical developments, prior rules, trends, or comparisons to clarify why the present proposal matters; score 0 when it provides no temporal or comparative context.
proposals.rationale: R24 compares decades of agency awareness with later technical studies, while R53 compares the proposed comment period with durations used for earlier complex proceedings.

proposals.name: Rule-text and authority precision
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accurately engages specific regulatory text, statutory provisions, standards, docket language, or related requirements and shows their relevance; score 0 when legal or technical references are absent or imprecise.
proposals.rationale: R35 identifies exact engine models and reconciles the proposal with a service bulletin, while R59 contrasts proposed regulatory language with statutory requirements and form instructions.

proposals.name: Issue-specific substance
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when nearly all of the comment contains docket-specific reasoning, evidence, or recommendations in the commenter’s own words; score 0 when it consists mainly of generic endorsement, opposition, credentials, or a procedural request.
proposals.rationale: R04 primarily offers generic organizational support and broad benefits, while R20 mainly requests more time despite describing the guidance’s complexity; by contrast, R11 and R59 contain detailed issue-specific material.

proposals.name: Balanced tradeoff reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment acknowledges competing interests or costs and explains why its recommendation best balances them; score 0 when it presents only one-sided advocacy without recognizing any countervailing concern.
proposals.rationale: R48 weighs recreational and commercial fishing interests alongside habitat protection, while R29 pairs aviation innovation and competitiveness with safety oversight and regulatory harmonization.

proposals.name: Institutional identity markers
proposals.instruction: How much does the text explicitly identify an institution, office, employer, membership base, executive title, or official representative role? Score only the extent of these markers from 0–10; do not judge whether the affiliation or comment is good.
proposals.rationale: Institutional reputation and resources can affect reception while also enabling genuine work. Explicit organizational identities appear in R07, R23, and R54, but identity itself is not substantive quality.

proposals.name: Formal document conventions
proposals.instruction: How much does the text use formal legal or regulatory document conventions such as letterhead, docket blocks, formal salutations, signature blocks, page numbering, and submission instructions? Score only their extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the conventions are good.
proposals.rationale: Professional assistance can improve both presentation and substantive accuracy, making this a mixed nuisance. Formal conventions are prominent in R01, R15, and R49.

proposals.name: Citation apparatus
proposals.instruction: How much does the text contain footnotes, statutory or regulatory citations, named studies, numbered references, hyperlinks, or other source-attribution devices? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the sources or citations are good.
proposals.rationale: Research support may generate both citation density and genuinely better analysis. Citation apparatus is visible in R03, R24, and R36, but the apparatus alone is not substantive quality.

proposals.name: Coalition breadth
proposals.instruction: How much does the text explicitly present multiple organizations, joint commenters, members, constituencies, or a representational mandate? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the coalition is legitimate or whether its position is good.
proposals.rationale: Networks can increase resources and coordination while also supplying broader substantive input. Coalition fingerprints appear in R24, R40, and R56.

proposals.name: Submission artifacts
proposals.instruction: How much does the text contain visible submission or file-ingestion artifacts such as attachment notices, email metadata, OCR errors, scan remnants, duplicated material, image text, or corrupted characters? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the artifacts improve or impair the comment.
proposals.rationale: Workflow and file-conversion artifacts can systematically shape the visible text without representing the author's substance. They appear in R02, R18, R36, and R41.

proposals.name: Textual volume and structure
proposals.instruction: How much textual volume and structural elaboration is present, including long passages, numerous paragraphs, headings, numbered sections, page markers, or multi-part organization? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the amount or structure is good.
proposals.rationale: Length and formatting can act as superficial proxies for effort or importance without establishing substantive quality. The contrast between highly structured material in R12 and R44 and very short comments such as R21 illustrates this channel.

proposals.name: Boilerplate language
proposals.instruction: How much of the text consists of stock openings, closings, recurring organizational descriptions, formulaic requests, or repeated passages? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the boilerplate is appropriate or good.
proposals.rationale: Coordinated communications can produce recurring language that is predictive of reception while adding no independent substantive signal. Repeated organizational wording appears across R10 and R34, and duplicated template material appears in R52.

proposals.name: Personal and local grounding
proposals.instruction: How much does the text contain first-person experience, personal role descriptions, local residence, place-specific activity, or direct involvement with the affected subject? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the experience makes the comment good.
proposals.rationale: Direct experience may both influence reception and contribute genuinely relevant knowledge, so this belongs in a sensitivity band. Personal or local grounding appears in R05, R25, and R27.

proposals.name: Timing and urgency cues
proposals.instruction: How much does the text explicitly mention deadlines, extensions, recent events, production or submission dates, delay, urgency, or requests for swift action? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the timing or urgency is justified or good.
proposals.rationale: Timing can influence presentation and available preparation while also affecting substantive completeness. Explicit extension and deadline cues appear in R02, R22, and R26.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission timing and available preparation time

proposals.name: Specialized jargon density
proposals.instruction: How much does the text use field-specific acronyms, technical nomenclature, model numbers, specialized terms, or domain abbreviations? Score only the extent from 0–10; do not judge whether the terminology is correct, useful, or good.
proposals.rationale: Specialized roles can produce jargon and may also support genuine substantive expertise, making this a mixed nuisance. Dense technical terminology appears in R06, R20, and R31.

proposals.name: Issue-Specific Anchoring
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment precisely identifies and analyzes particular proposed provisions, sections, definitions, or assumptions; score 0 when it addresses only the broad topic or agency generally.
proposals.rationale: R03 discusses UB-04 billing and PS&R treatment, while R26 identifies exact engine models and applicability language.

proposals.name: Causal Mechanism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment clearly traces how the proposal would produce concrete effects through a plausible chain of events; score 0 when it merely asserts that the proposal is good or bad.
proposals.rationale: R02 explains why closing federal waters would not address nearshore fishing, and R22 links payment changes to access, staffing, utilization, and costs.

proposals.name: Actionable Textual Change
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies precise replacement language, edits, or an unambiguous regulatory change; score 0 when it offers only a general request without specifying what text or requirement should change.
proposals.rationale: R25 proposes detailed amended regulatory language, and R33 gives ten structured edits including replacement wording.

proposals.name: Implementation Realism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment anticipates operational constraints, failure modes, resources, documentation, or workflows needed to implement the proposal; score 0 when it ignores practical implementation entirely.
proposals.rationale: R34 analyzes HVAC failures, power transitions, testing burdens, and acceptable documentation, while R60 identifies concrete ambulance equipment and funding constraints.

proposals.name: Evidence Traceability
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when important factual claims are tied to identifiable studies, datasets, official records, calculations, or citations; score 0 when factual assertions have no traceable support.
proposals.rationale: R09 identifies FARS, specific query procedures, and correction-factor sources, while R39 supplies agency statistics and numbered source references.

proposals.name: Quantitative Calibration
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when numerical facts are used accurately to establish magnitude, compare alternatives, or substantiate a burden or benefit; score 0 when numbers are absent or presented without interpretable context.
proposals.rationale: R02 compares the proposed 13,000-pound limit with a 21,139-pound historical average, and R07 compares permitted lead concentrations with the 90-ppm limit for other products.

proposals.name: Firsthand Operational Knowledge
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the author connects direct professional, geographic, cultural, or experiential knowledge to specific policy effects; score 0 when claimed identity or experience is unrelated to the analysis.
proposals.rationale: R23 connects 150 days on the water and specific fishing locations to habitat impacts, while R60 draws on Louisiana EMS system responsibilities and practitioner conditions.

proposals.name: Regulatory Coherence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains how the proposal should interact with existing rules, standards, guidance, forms, or related proceedings; score 0 when it treats the proposal in isolation.
proposals.rationale: R16 recommends harmonizing electric-engine requirements across certification regimes, and R56 compares the proposed directive with a specific service bulletin and related directive.

proposals.name: Constructive Alternatives
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment offers a feasible alternative, safeguard, phased approach, pilot, exemption, or fallback that addresses the identified problem; score 0 when it provides only opposition or support.
